correctness.rationale: For each class member the uniquely smallest cyclic one-run determines a unique lexicographic root. The first letter difference versus every competing zero-root is at zero-based offset a+1 and alternating order favors the lex root iff a is odd. Rooted cyclic-gap compositions give the two rational summand series without any orbit division; unique root implies primitivity. Positivity and elementary pole analysis establish the two dominant exponential terms; Lucas enumeration bounds global coincidences. Direct exhaustive independently coded testing covers all binary words of lengths 1..18 and the global necessary condition to 14, and does not substitute for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted result is the two exact all-length enumerative generating series and opposed quantitative conditional/global density laws for a canonically rooted class of binary necklaces. Prior work completely covers algorithms for rotating Galois words and much of their membership characterization, which is explicitly credited. The inspected primary sections neither state the enumerations nor imply the specific quantitative formula as an immediate displayed corollary; they furnish broader possible routes to the parity sublemma, which is not claimed in isolation. Remaining literature incompleteness is an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: General 2024 hybrid-Lyndon characterization may have unindexed enumerative consequences, and same counts may exist in unindexed combinatorics-on-words literature.
The gap-uniqueness restriction is essential: tied-shortest-gap cases are not classified by this theorem; novelty and value hinge on quantitative enumeration, not the parity sublemma alone.
Finite exhaustive checking cannot independently audit singularity arguments or the global infinite counting claims.

value.rationale: Both canonical rotations are core invariants underlying ordinary and alternating Burrows–Wheeler transforms. The unique minimal cyclic gap is an intrinsic, non-arbitrary anchor that makes an otherwise ambiguous rotational-order comparison analytically accessible. The result completely enumerates a natural infinite class and establishes a nontrivial asymptotic paradox: agreement tends to one exponentially within this family but decays exponentially globally. It supplies exact benchmark sequences and exponential rates without claiming a complete characterization outside the stipulated family.
